classification: research screening, not new proof strategy established

proposals.name: Theta modular cancellation behind the circle map
proposals.status: exploratory mechanism search only; first sufficient sublemma rejected
proposals.wall_check: Same open gap for the full radial-growth criterion; distinct first theta-slice test now failed
proposals.scope_comparison: No dependence on the NS98 selected-direction cost. This concerns actual entire-function zero rigidity. Neither equal circle counts nor a Gram geometry controls the radial derivative.
proposals.new_input_required: An explicit positive autocorrelation decomposition of the full integrated theta-product kernel, obtained from the actual Jacobi modular identity without presupposing Fourier positivity. The kernel is K_x(t)=integral_0^infinity p*sinh(2*x*p)*phi(p+t)*phi(p-t) dp.
proposals.first_falsifiable_test: Test the stronger claim that every fixed-p slice has nonnegative cosine transform. A_0(20) is strictly negative, with complete tails and 256/384-bit/cutoff replay; continuity extends failure to some p>0.
proposals.next_bounded_task: Before any numerical scan, attempt a symbolic modular-resummation factorization for the integrated kernel or its first x-Taylor coefficient K_1(t)=integral_R p^2*phi(p+t)*phi(p-t) dp. The K_1 criterion itself is classical, and proving it alone would be only a necessary-condition result.
proposals.continue_if: A concrete candidate factor or signed identity is derived from theta data, rejects the off-line controls, and has a fully stated domain/tail argument. Then test that identity before attempting a cofinal proof.
proposals.stop_if: Only the Cayley map, an RH-equivalent sign restatement, generic log-concavity, a square root of an unproved nonnegative Fourier transform, or per-slice positivity is offered.
proposals.novelty: A possible new-to-repo mechanism search, not a new criterion; no surviving new inequality established.

proposals.name: A backward-in-shift Jensen interlacing mechanism
proposals.status: deprioritized; no mechanism supplied and modest-degree scans are prior art
proposals.wall_check: Same open gap in the classical hyperbolicity program; distinct from NS98 cost
proposals.scope_comparison: This is not the closed direct rational-Li/finite-window identification. It uses the exact theta moments and their high-order relation.
proposals.new_input_required: An arithmetic rule on gamma(n) that propagates real-rootedness from the known large-shift region to all lower shifts at unbounded degree, rather than positivity or log-concavity of a generic sequence.
proposals.first_falsifiable_test: Write a coefficient-explicit interlacing or stability-preserving relation for J^(d,n) and J^(d,n+1); check it against exact non-real-rooted symmetric controls before a zeta calculation. No such relation is proved here.
proposals.continue_if: A concrete unbounded-degree propagation inequality is identified that is not implied by the already known fixed-degree asymptotic.
proposals.stop_if: The proposal only verifies modest degrees, invokes eventual fixed-degree hyperbolicity, or assumes the desired interlacing.
proposals.literature_screen: The 2022 paper already proves n>=c*exp(d/2), and (using its cited finite-height verification) all n for d<=9.36e20. These are sufficient regions, not exact current global frontiers or RH.
proposals.novelty: Classical program. No claim that a backward-shift strategy or this problem is globally new.

recommendation: Do not announce a new RH route. If continuing geometry, require an explicit theta-specific integrated factorization first; the tested per-slice shortcut must stop.
excluded_repeats: unrestricted PSD LCM cone or free trace normalization (NS96/97)
Clifford coordinate changes without a CAE bound (NS47/50)
continuous closure substituted for integer closure (NS76)
absolute residual or finite ground-zero proximity substituted for CCM selection (NS43)
